content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": true, "main_gap": "none", "errors": [{"description": "Step 2 justifies 'P > 1 always' by the claim that a positive integer that never increases and starts above 1 can never reach 1 — this is false (e.g. 4→2→1). The intended fact is trivial (the new pair has product lcm(m,n) ≥ 2, so a move never creates two 1's), and the summary section states this correct reason, but the formal proof's stated justification is invalid.", "quote": "A positive integer that never increases and starts above $1$ can never reach $1$; hence $P > 1$ after any number of moves."}], "notes": "Termination via (product, number of ones) is correct and well-bounded. Part (b) invariant gcd of p-adic valuations, with the (min, |difference|) Euclidean step, is proven carefully including the all-zero case; the final formula for M is correct. Only flaw is the invalid one-line justification in Step 2, easily fixed."}
